title: Workers AI Adds New Models for Voice, Vision, and Data Extraction
summary: Cloudflare Workers AI now offers PhoneLLM Mini for real‑time voice tasks, Clef‑omni for multimodal audio/video input, and Clairic for structured data extraction, expanding edge AI capabilities.

sections.heading: Today's AI Overview
sections.body: Edge AI is moving beyond simple inference to support real‑time, multimodal tasks directly in browsers and serverless functions. Recent updates from Cloudflare Workers AI illustrate this shift, adding lightweight models that handle voice, video, and structured extraction without leaving the edge.

sections.heading: Deep Dive: New Workers AI Models
sections.body: Three new models expand what developers can do at the edge. @cf/daily-co/phonellm-mini‑alpha‑2 (PhoneLLM Mini) provides fast speech‑to‑text and LLM‑level dialogue for phone‑call scenarios. @cf/cloudflare/clef‑omni now supports audio (WAV/MP3) and video (MP4/WebM) alongside existing text and image inputs, enabling multimodal context in a single request. Finally, Clairic offers a preview extraction model for typed key‑value pairs, with open‑weights planned for future release. All three are accessible via Workers AI, lowering deployment complexity and cost compared to hosted alternatives. Source: Cloudflare Workers AI changelogs.

sections.heading: Today's Prompt
sections.prompt_body: You are given a PDF or plain‑text document containing labeled fields (e.g., invoice number, date, amount). Using the Clairic model, output a JSON object where each field name maps to its extracted value. If a field is missing, set it to null. Preserve original formatting for dates and numbers.
sections.prompt_usecase: Paste the document content into a Workers AI request, call the Clairic endpoint, and parse the returned JSON directly into your application for downstream processing.

sections.heading: Wow! This Week's Viral AI News
sections.body: OpenAI announced the GPT‑Rosalind Academic Plan, granting eligible research labs sponsor‑level access to GPT‑Rosalind and accompanying tools for life‑science research. The initiative lowers barriers for academic teams to apply large language models to genomics and bioinformatics, potentially accelerating discoveries in the public domain. Source: OpenAI Blog.
sections.source_title: OpenAI Blog – Introducing the Rosalind Academic Plan

sections.heading: Practical: Applying Workers AI in Customer Support
sections.body: Build a real‑time support agent that first transcribes a caller’s audio using PhoneLLM Mini, then enriches the context with any video frames captured via Clef‑omni (e.g., product images), and finally extracts actionable data (customer ID, issue type) with Clairic. All steps run in the edge function, reducing latency and avoiding data transfer to third‑party APIs.

sections.heading: Weekly Watch: Edge‑First Multimodal AI
sections.body: The trend is clear: multimodal models are being optimized for low‑latency edge deployment. Cloudflare’s additions show how voice, video, and structured extraction can be combined in serverless environments. Simultaneously, academic collaborations (e.g., OpenAI’s Rosalind plan) democratize access to powerful LLMs, suggesting a future where research and production AI converge more tightly.
